title: Estimate one tensor's storage
prompt: Implement `tensor_bytes(shape, bytes_per_element=4)` by multiplying dimensions and element size. This estimates one dense tensor, not peak training memory. Example `(32,20,128)` float32 needs 327680 bytes.
tests:
assert tensor_bytes((32,20,128))==327680, 'Count all tensor elements times four bytes'
assert tensor_bytes((2,3),8)==48, 'Respect the element size'
assert tensor_bytes((0,3))==0, 'An empty dimension stores no elements'
assert tensor_bytes(())==4, 'A scalar tensor has one element'
hint: Start the product at one, even for an empty shape tuple.
solution:
def tensor_bytes(shape,bytes_per_element=4):
    count=1
    for n in shape: count*=n
    return count*bytes_per_element

title: Weight an uneven final chunk
prompt: Implement `batch_mean(means, sizes)` for nonempty matching lists with positive sizes. Example means `[1,3,5]`, sizes `[4,4,2]` gives 2.6.
tests:
assert abs(batch_mean([1,3,5],[4,4,2])-2.6)<1e-10, 'Do not overweight the last two rows'
assert batch_mean([2,8],[1,3])==6.5, 'Use every row in the denominator'
assert batch_mean([4],[7])==4, 'A single chunk keeps its mean'
hint: Sum mean*size, then divide by total size.
solution:
def batch_mean(means,sizes):
    return sum(m*n for m,n in zip(means,sizes))/sum(sizes)

tests:
from torch import nn
import copy
torch.set_num_threads(1)
torch.manual_seed(9)
a=nn.Linear(2,1);b=copy.deepcopy(a)
x=torch.tensor([[1.,2.],[0.,1.],[2.,-1.],[3.,2.],[-1.,4.]])
y=torch.tensor([[1.],[2.],[0.],[3.],[-2.]])
((a(x)-y)**2).mean().backward()
before=[p.detach().clone() for p in b.parameters()]
accumulate(b,x,y,2)
assert all(p.grad is not None for p in b.parameters()), 'Backpropagate each weighted chunk'
assert all(torch.allclose(p.grad,q.grad,atol=1e-6,rtol=1e-6) for p,q in zip(a.parameters(),b.parameters())), 'Uneven chunks must match full-batch gradients'
assert all(torch.equal(old,p) for old,p in zip(before,b.parameters())), 'Accumulate gradients without updating parameters'
hint: Use len(xb)/len(x) before backward; leave zero_grad outside the loop.
solution:
import torch

def accumulate(model,x,y,micro):
    model.zero_grad()
    for start in range(0,len(x),micro):
        xb=x[start:start+micro];yb=y[start:start+micro]
        loss=((model(xb)-yb)**2).mean()
        (loss*len(xb)/len(x)).backward()

title: Bound the total speedup
prompt: Implement `overall_speedup(fraction, component_speedup)` using Amdahl's law. Assume fraction in [0,1] and positive speedup. Example accelerating 20% of the work by 2x gives approximately 1.111x overall.
tests:
assert abs(overall_speedup(0.2,2)-1/0.9)<1e-10, 'Include the unchanged 80 percent'
assert overall_speedup(0,100)==1, 'Speeding up no work has no benefit'
assert overall_speedup(1,4)==4, 'If all work improves, total speedup matches it'
